title: stopWords
summary: Return common stop words for supported Text Analytics languages.

gpu_support.notes: `stopWords` returns host-resident string metadata and does not use provider kernels.

description: `stopWords` returns a column string array of common stop words. `stopWords('Language', language)` selects English (`'en'`), Japanese (`'ja'`), German (`'de'`), or Korean (`'ko'`).
behaviors: `stopWords` with no inputs returns the English stop-word list.
`stopWords('Language', language)` accepts scalar string or character-vector option values.
The supported language codes are `en`, `ja`, `de`, and `ko`, matching the Text Analytics Toolbox language set for this function.
The output is a string column vector with shape `N x 1`.

RunMat provides compatibility stop-word lists for the documented languages. The list contents cover common function use such as building removal sets for text preprocessing; exact release-to-release MathWorks vocabulary identity is not guaranteed.
Tokenized-document removal helpers such as `removeStopWords` and custom token deletion remain part of the broader Text Analytics object surface.

examples.description: Use Stop Words In A Custom Filter
examples.output: `custom` is a string column vector suitable for text-preprocessing workflows.

faqs.question: Which language codes are accepted?
faqs.answer: `en`, `ja`, `de`, and `ko` are accepted. Other language codes raise `RunMat:stopWords:InvalidInput`.

faqs.question: Is this tied to tokenizedDocument?
faqs.answer: No. `stopWords` is a standalone list function. Tokenized-document operations that consume these lists remain tracked separately in the Text Analytics compatibility issue.

faqs.question: Does `stopWords` execute on the GPU?
faqs.answer: No. It returns host string metadata, so no `runmat-accelerate` provider path is involved.

points: The option name is case-insensitive and must be `Language`.

gpu_residency: `stopWords` returns host-resident strings and has no provider kernel.
